newsitem.title: BELGIUM: TENNIS-ENQVIST FALLS AT FIRST HURDLE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ENQVIST FALLS AT FIRST HURDLE.

text.p: Thomas Enqvist, who won a tournament in Marseille on Sunday, was brought down to earth on Wednesday when he was knocked out in the first round of the European Community championship by Spain's Francisco Clavet.
The Swedish third seed was beaten 4-6 7-6 6-3 by clay-court specialist Clavet on the Antwerp indoor carpet surface.

But second seed Marcelo Rios, forced by injury to pull out of the Marseille final against Enqvist in the second set, came through the first round without mishap by trouncing Romanian Adrian Voinea 6-1 6-4.

Rios, the highest ranking player in this tournament following the withdrawal of top seed Goran Ivanisevic on Tuesday, withdrew in Marseille with a strained quadriceps muscle but was declared fit to play here after treatment by a physiotherapist.
Enqvist took the first set but landed himself in trouble when he lost the second set tie-break 7-4.
His concentration was further undermined by some questionable line calls in the final set which prompted him to remonstrate with the chair umpire.
"I'd rather not talk about it," Enqvist said of his discussions with the umpire.
But he said he felt mentally tired after having played singles and doubles in Marseille, something he said he had never done before.
"I had my chances in the second set but Clavet was too good then," he said. "Also the balls were very different here. I didn't feel the ball well."
World number six Rios produced near flawless tennis in the first set of his match against Voinea which featured some breath-taking rallies.
Rios fell 2-0 behind early in the second set but quickly fought back to win in just over an hour.
"I was feeling good today...but it hurts a little bit. I have to see how I feel tomorrow," said Rios, who said he had been treated twice a day by a physiotherapist for the past five days.

Rios, who meets Martin Damm of the Czech Republic in the second round, denied that organisers had put extra pressure on him after the injury-enforced withdrawals of former Wimbledon champion Boris Becker and Ivanisevic on Tuesday.

Rios, who started out as a clay-court specialist, said he would also compete on grass this year and play at Wimbledon. His only previous experience of Wimbledon was in 1995 when he was beaten in the first round.
"If you are a top player you have to play on every surface. I try to be good on every surface," he said.
Former Olympic champion Marc Rosset of Switzerland earlier became the first player to reach the quarter-finals after coming from behind to beat German qualifier Nicolas Kiefer 3-6 6-3 6-1.
Kiefer called for a doctor early in the final set because of stomach cramps before playing on.
